name: sitecheck
description: Check one public web page and get scores and a list of fixes in priority order.

interface.shortDescription: Find what to fix on a website
interface.longDescription:
SiteCheck checks one public web page at a time and tells you what to fix first. Give it an address and it returns scores for speed, accessibility, search preview (basic SEO), social preview and hygiene (security and server settings), plus one list of fixes ordered by importance. Each fix says what to do and whether it takes minutes, takes hours or needs a developer.

Speed figures come from Google PageSpeed Insights and the Chrome UX Report. Accessibility rules come from axe-core. Automated checks find only some problems, and a result is not a legal compliance check.

You can also preview how a draft title, description and image will look in Google and on social media before a page is published.

SiteCheck checks only the page you name and does not crawl a site. Site owners can opt out through robots.txt, a meta tag or e-mail. A site whose robots.txt blocks all bots is not checked. Each result is saved at a public report link, and no account is needed.
defaultPrompt: Check my website and tell me what to fix first.
How fast does this page load, and what should I fix?
How will this page look when it is shared?

positive.description: A full check of a public page, asking for priorities. The result may be reused if the page was scanned in the last 24 hours.
positive.prompt: Use SiteCheck to check sitecheck.datacleave.com and tell me what to fix first.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check_site once for sitecheck.datacleave.com on the mobile profile. The card shows five scores (speed, accessibility, search preview, social preview, hygiene) and a Fix first list. On 2026-11-04 the scores were 98, 100, 100, 100 and 95 with 3 fixes, led by files that hold up the first view of the page. If the page was scanned in the last 24 hours the card says how old the result is and offers Rescan. The reply gives the scores and top fixes and links the report.

positive.description: A check on the desktop profile, passed because the user asks for it.
positive.prompt: Use SiteCheck to check kinpress.datacleave.com on desktop.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check_site once with device desktop. The card is marked Desktop and shows five scores and a Fix first list. On 2026-11-04 the scores were 95, 100, 76, 29 and 95 with 13 fixes, led by missing og:image, og:title and twitter:card. The card shows five of them and links the full report. A result under 24 hours old is reused and the card says so.

positive.description: A question about how a page looks in search results and when shared.
positive.prompt: Use SiteCheck to see how doko.datacleave.com looks in Google and when shared on social media.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check_site once on the mobile profile. The card shows five scores and a Fix first list. On 2026-11-04 search preview was 88 and social preview was 29, with missing og:image and og:title among the top fixes. The reply answers about Google and social sharing. On a new scan the speed test may still be running when the reply is written, and the reply says so; the card updates by itself when it finishes.

positive.description: A draft share card for a page that does not exist yet. No page is scanned; only the named image is fetched.
positive.prompt: Use SiteCheck to preview a share card with the title 'Spring opening hours', the description 'Open every day from 9 to 5 starting in April.' and the image https://sitecheck.datacleave.com/static/og.png
positive.expected_behavior: Calls preview_meta once and runs no scan. The card is headed Share preview and shows five previews: Google (title, address and description, no image), Facebook, X and Slack (image, title and description) and LinkedIn (image and title, no description, by design). The image is the blue SiteCheck share image. The reply confirms the values used.

positive.description: A request for a saved report, with no new scan. Run the first case first if no scan of this site exists.
positive.prompt: Use SiteCheck to show the saved report it already has for sitecheck.datacleave.com. Do not run a new scan.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_report once and does not call check_site. The tool step reads Opened Get a scan report. The card shows the saved report for sitecheck.datacleave.com with five scores, a Fix first list and how old the result is. If no scan exists, the tool says none was found and asks for check_site to be run first.

negative.description: A definition with no page named. SiteCheck has nothing to scan and must not be called; ChatGPT explains in its own words.
negative.prompt: What does Largest Contentful Paint mean?

negative.description: General writing advice with no page named. SiteCheck must not be called.
negative.prompt: How do I write a good meta description?

negative.description: A choice between platforms with no page to check. SiteCheck must not be called.
negative.prompt: Should a small shop use Shopify or WordPress?

review.commerce_description: SiteCheck does not sell products, take payments or process transactions.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: check one public web page, get scores and a list of fixes in priority order, and preview draft share cards.
